note: All 153 pivots are Early Modern Irish prose, mostly devotional and hagiographic (Desiderius-type dialogues, saints lives of Declan, Finan, Fechin, Senan, Tundal), with partners mainly Greek medical/historical prose. No defensible inherited phraseology found. Leads examined and rejected: BC-6622d Finan heals a horse leg (gur leanadar a cnamha da cheile), which echoes the IE horse-leg charm motif (Merseburg II, AV 4.12) but has no congruent partner in the slab (only Galen/Hippocrates anatomy with knemē) and no cognate formula; BC-a1d82 do lethnaigh a ainm agus a clu (fame spread broad, cf. pṛthu śravas / kleos eury), no second-branch anchor in the slab; BC-91d8c kneeling prayer (do lec a gluine ... do ghuidh ~ OHG Tatian giboganemo kneuue betota), which is Biblical genuflexion and not inherited.
